speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West): Mr Speaker, I must thank Members for staying back for this Adjournment Motion despite this late hour.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In this Adjournment Motion, I will outline the significance of the problem of microplastics, the need for sacrifice from all of us to address it and to propose two carrots that the Government could implement, to reduce single-use plastics.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Doing so will not only be good for the environment, it will make a material impact on our health.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Plastics are artificial beings called into reality by humans – often, they are used only once, but live forever.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we are living with the disastrous consequences of global plastic waste because of its non-biodegradable nature.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Plastics poses a significant threat to wildlife, when animals ingest plastics debris.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Production of plastics relies heavily on fossil fuels and contributes significant greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Burning plastics releases toxic chemicals into the environment.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The damage to our health from microplastics leeching is even more urgent and deadly.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Microplastics enter our body because of what we eat and drink, we breathe them in and absorb them through skin contact.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some researchers show that we are probably ingesting the weight of a plastic credit card every week without realising it.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: When we drink from low quality, single-use plastic cups or microwave food wrapped in plastics, we are sprinkling microplastics into our food and drinks.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While the research on microplastics and their health impact is still developing, there is significant evidence that microplastics are related to health issues in the gastrointestinal, respiratory, reproductive, cardiovascular and autoimmune systems.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: According to a recent release by Harvard School of Public Health, microplastic exposure can lead to damage to cells, DNA and the immune response.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Observational studies have shown an association of microplastics with increased risk of heart attack, stroke, dementia, or early death.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We need action on two fronts: first, internationally, everyone on this planet – countries, businesses, people – need to limit plastic pollution and to find environmentally-safe alternatives; second, on the individual, consumer front – we can and should make changes to our habits and lifestyle, to reduce the use of single-use plastics in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Here, let me speak about the two carrots.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The first carrot is to incentivise re-use of plastics.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, let me talk about why reuse and not recycle.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Re-use is always greener than recycle, but in the case of plastics, especially so.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This single digit phenomenon is not just prevalent in Singapore but in the United States and many countries as well.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is not the fault of the National Environment Agency (NEA) nor Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is an intractable economics problem because it simply costs more to recycle than to produce new plastic products.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Since plastics recycling rate is very low at around 5%, even if we double plastics recycling, nine in 10 items will still become trash.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, there is an urgent need to step up upstream prevention.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And this is the real solution in the long run.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Economics also fails for single-use plastics because the price does not reflect its true cost.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Because when we include the cost of removal, to collect, transport and burn, plus the cost of carbon emissions to the environment, the real costs are actually much higher.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is just that they are unpriced, or not paid directly by consumers, unless we count the price of poor health.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Government, businesses and communities can work together to encourage and incentivise businesses to offer re-use solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In every household, many consumer items can be stored in re-usable containers.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If there are more options for refills stations for common household items such as laundry detergents, dishwashing liquids, or even hair and body shampoos, especially if they are offered at a discounted price, consumers will be motivated to switch to reuseable options.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This shift in consumer behaviour would directly cut down the usage of single-use plastics.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One good ground-up commercial solution is the EcoWorks vending machines that dispense laundry detergent and washing liquids.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The residents of my colleagues, Mr Foo Cexiang, Ms Valerie Yap, Mr Ng Shi Xuan and myself, have been enjoying the convenience and cost savings from refilling laundry detergents and washing liquids into their own bottles.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I call for the Government to do more to support start-ups with environmentally-friendly and commercially scalable ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Currently, NEA’s 3R instruments have strong collection and recycling levers.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The 3R Fund, Eco Fund and related grant schemes should also recognise measurable avoidance, so prevention is funded on outcomes, just like in the case of recycling tonnage.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government could consider reclassifying some of these recycling points into reuse or refill points as waste-prevention infrastructure, so that public sites can host them under green allocations.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Such reuse or refilling points would help to reduce packaging upstream, avoiding what would otherwise go into the blue recycling bins or the green general-waste bins.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope the Minister for Sustainability and Environment will consider this request and review the scope of its incentive schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The second carrot is to incentivise BYO – or the acronym for “Bring Your Own”.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Businesses in support of sustainability have put their money where their mouth is, to reduce single-use plastic cups.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This practice is a four-time winner because customers save money, businesses enjoy green branding, Government spend less on waste collection and incineration, and toxic waste and CO2 on our planet is reduced.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In August, a BYO campaign was started in the National University of Singapore (NUS) campus to encourage the community to bring their own cups, bottles and tumblers.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Previously, a takeaway drink would cost $1.70, whereas it is now $1.90 if a disposable cup is used.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If one brings his or her own cup, one would get a 60-cent discount, making it $1.30.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This BYO campaign is supported by all nine food courts and canteens across the entire campus.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Three months in, many students have started to bring their own cups, so they do feel that this discount has incentivised them to reduce plastic waste and they are quite happy about the money they are saving!

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is a positive example of how concerted efforts by NUS and their business partners can change consumer behaviour.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government and businesses can certainly do a lot more to accelerate the BYO movement.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I would call for all our coffee shop and food court chains, to join in this BYO movement, to give a discount to customers who bring their own cups.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: After all, for every cup that is not used, the drink stalls will also save on their operating costs.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government could also encourage large F&B chains and public venues such as malls, campuses and hawker centres to adopt returnable cups and containers for dine-in customers.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Where feasible, they should track return rate and litter reduction metrics.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government can give a carrot to reward businesses that are pro-health and pro-environment.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This carrot will hardly cost the Government any resource.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I would ask the Singapore Food Agency to consider adding a new criterion in their Food Hygiene Recognition Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: A Green Mark rating could be given to F&B operators that adopt environmentally-friendly measures such as offering BYO discounts to customers or use sustainable packaging materials.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This Green Mark rating will be an effective differentiator for discerning customers who care about the planet and their health and saving some money will be a bonus.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hopefully, over time there will be fewer plastic bottles and metal cans trash on our streets.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also need to drive greater consumer awareness about the harmful impact of single-use plastics, to both our environment and our health.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Perhaps what we need now is a new slogan to reignite the BYO movement.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It could go like this: BYO: A Greener Planet, A Healthier You.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The streets and the lakes are clean and there was hardly any trash.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In cafes and supermarkets, few items were placed inside plastic containers.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: People bring along their own cups and bottles.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The BYO culture is a big part of the Swiss society.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Back in 1984, our then Prime Minister Mr Goh Chok Tong, had set a target for Singapore to meet the Swiss standard of living.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In terms of gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, we have indeed caught up with the Swiss.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But in terms of our respect for the environment, I think we will need to do more.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope our Government and our people will continue to strive towards the Swiss standard of sustainability.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, a standard of living would be better measured in health and sustainability than it is by GDP, because all the wealth in the world cannot buy back ruined health nor a damaged environment.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope the Government will carefully consider my two proposals.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In fact, we should continue to incentivise and implement more good ideas that will drive the reduction of single-use plastics in our society.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Additionally, with less trash generated, the cost of waste collection and incineration will reduce.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The savings should be ploughed back to promote more circular economy solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This move will not come without sacrifice – inconvenience, time spent, old habits disrupted, new behaviour and change is seldom welcome.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every big change starts with a single small act.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I choose good health and a green environment, over the convenience of single-use plastics.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope more Singaporeans will make the same choice.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And I call for our Government to make the right policies that will help people make the right choice.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Because the real carrots are not the two small ones I have outlined, but the innumerable benefits we reap in good health and a green planet.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary): Mr Speaker, I thank Ms Poh Li San for her interest, her passion and her hard work on this important issue and for urging us all to reduce our plastic waste.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We share her concerns about the impact of waste and plastic waste in particular, and welcome her efforts to reduce, reuse and recycle.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: She has highlighted areas where we can as a society do more, and she has also made it clear that a key shift is necessary in our behaviour.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In my speech I will highlight the efforts that we are already making, as well as programme funding that already supports initiatives to reduce waste.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I would urge Members of the House to encourage further participation in these programmes by community stakeholders.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Each country has its own unique context and challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In Singapore, we have a robust waste management system.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: All of our plastic waste is collected for disposal or recycling.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Any waste that cannot be recycled is treated at our waste-to-energy incineration plants before the ash is sent to Semakau Landfill.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This robust waste management system and our strict anti-littering regulations limit the leakage of plastic waste into our environment.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One study found that about 97% of plastic waste found on Singapore’s beaches originate from offshore sources.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Poh Li San has a concern about the potential health impact of microplastics that leak into our environment.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NEA, Public Utilities Board and the Singapore Food Agency regularly monitor the latest scientific developments on this issue.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our agencies are also monitoring the levels of microplastics in our drinking water and our food.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While we have been successful in limiting the leakage of plastics into the environment, managing our consumption and disposal of plastics remains a challenge.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This in turn results in carbon emissions when we incinerate plastic waste.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, plastics serve many useful functions and some will continue to be essential to our daily lives.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, plastic packaging protects goods such as fresh foods from moisture, contamination and damage.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In our daily lives, many of us also use plastic bags to dispose of our household waste.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is why our approach has been to reduce the use of disposables, minimise irresponsible consumption and improper disposal, and encourage reuse and recycling as much as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In line with this approach, the Government has implemented several initiatives to promote individual behavioural change and help industry become more sustainable.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Industry is another key partner in our efforts and we have a suite of measures to support industry in adopting and scaling up more sustainable practices.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To build industry capability, we launched the Packaging Partnership Programme (PPP) in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Under this programme, NEA conducts regular outreach sessions and training, supporting companies in adopting sustainable packaging waste management practices, such as improved design to optimise packaging size and weight.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have seen industry players stepping up in response.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In March this year, the Alliance for Action on Packaging Waste Reduction for the E-commerce Sector, which comprises 14 companies across the e-commerce supply chain, published a set of practical guidelines on sustainable e-commerce packaging.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The guidelines provide a comprehensive list of practical 3R solutions for e-commerce.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is a much-needed resource given the rapid growth of e-commerce in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Reducing plastic waste is a shared mission and this requires the participation of everyone.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened to hear Ms Poh’s two suggestions to incentivise re-use and encourage BYO.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have worked with community members, non-governmental organisations and businesses to implement similar ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To encourage more ground-up initiatives, we launched the SG Eco Fund in 2020 to support community projects that aim to advance environmental sustainability, including those that reduce, reuse and recycle waste.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SG Eco Fund complements other sources of funding provided by NEA, including the Closing the Resource Loop Funding Initiative which promotes research and development on resource recovery solutions, and the 3R Fund which supports organisations in the implementation of projects that reduce waste generation by promoting reuse or recycling systems.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am glad to hear that Ms Poh Li San and her colleagues are actively supporting ground-up commercial solutions that promote reuse, such as refill services for laundry detergent.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One example is Muuse, which ran a pilot project to provide reusable containers for customers at a hawker centre.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If you have more of such innovative sustainability ideas that can benefit the community, I encourage you to apply for the SG Eco Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The idea of encouraging BYO is a good one.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Small changes in habits can have a big impact when adopted widely.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We seek everyone’s support to participate actively and make this scheme a success.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Choices to cultivate new habits and choices to adopt greener practices.

speaker: The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With the right mindset, habits and systems in place, we can build a more sustainable Singapore together.
